title: Communication and the communication management approach
blurb: Explain why communication matters, the purpose of the communication management approach, what goes under each of its main headings, and why it must be two-way.
question: A project will use a video meeting platform for its hybrid team. Under which heading of the communication management approach does this belong?

teach.body: Good communication avoids misconceptions and unnecessary barriers when changes are introduced. PRINCE2 7 handles it through the communication management approach, one of the nine management approaches and part of the PID. Formally, it defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, across the project ecosystem, supporting alignment and shaping of the project. In plain English: who hears what, how, how often, and how we listen back.

teach.caption: The approach engages stakeholders through a controlled, bidirectional flow of information (manual 3.4).

teach.h: Four headings you must be able to sort
head: Heading
What goes there
Example
rows: Who is impacted, and who can influence success
Per group: purpose, frequency, channel, message
People, time and money for communications
teach.caption: These four headings are the ones tested in official papers. Other typical headings exist, but learn these cold.

teach.h: Resistance tells you where to talk
teach.body: Pockets of resistance to the project are a useful indicator of where communication should be focused. The right response is to find out why a stakeholder resists, because they may have a valid concern, rather than sidelining them. How a team communicates also depends on whether it is co-located, remote or hybrid, so channels and formats should fit.

teach.h: Which heading does this item belong under?

children.edge: How often, which channel, what message
children.label: Schedule and procedures

items.label: Created in 'agree the management approaches'; part of the PID
Highlight reports at the frequency it sets
Reviewed and adapted as stakeholders change
Reviewed for closure: who needs to be told

teach.body: Penmarric Borough Council is installing self-service kiosks in its libraries. In initiation, project manager Laura Fenwick writes the communication management approach: stakeholder analysis (library staff, regular users, councillors, union rep Gareth Hughes); a schedule (weekly staff huddles, a monthly user newsletter, quarterly councillor briefings); tools (staff messaging platform, online survey); and resources (a comms officer one day a week). When Gareth opposes the kiosks, Laura meets him to understand his concerns about jobs and adjusts the staff messages.

teach.text: A communications platform, such as video meeting software, goes under supporting tools and techniques, not resources. And do not confuse approaches: the communication management approach plans communication and feedback; the change management approach plans the move to the target state; the issue management approach controls baseline changes.

items: Communication avoids misconceptions and unnecessary barriers to change (manual 3.4).
The communication management approach (part of the PID) defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem.
It sets up a controlled, bidirectional flow of information to engage stakeholders.
Tested headings: stakeholder analysis; communications schedule and procedures; supporting tools and techniques; resources.
Pockets of resistance show where to focus communication. Created in initiation, it sets highlight report frequency and is reviewed at stage boundaries and closure.

summary: You can now explain the purpose of the communication management approach, sort information under its four tested headings and use resistance as a signal for where to communicate. You can also say when the approach is created and reviewed.

A.q: What is the purpose of the communication management approach?
options: To describe how changes to the project baseline will be controlled
To set out how the organization moves from current to target state
To define the means and frequency of communication and feedback
To describe the quality techniques and standards for products
A.why: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, across the project ecosystem (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Controlling changes to the baseline is the job of the issue management approach.
whyNot.1: Moving from the current to the target state is the purpose of the change management approach.
whyNot.3: Quality techniques and standards are described in the quality management approach.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The communication management approach engages stakeholders through a controlled and [?] flow of information.
A.why: PRINCE2 describes a controlled and bidirectional flow of information, so feedback is received as well as messages sent (manual 3.4).

whyNot.1: Some information may be sensitive, but the defining feature is that the flow is two-way.
whyNot.2: The approach is about communication across the project ecosystem, not through a hierarchy.
whyNot.3: The flow is described as two-way, not as centralized.

A.q: Which management product contains the stakeholder analysis used to plan project communication?
A.why: Stakeholder analysis is one of the headings of the communication management approach (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: The risk register records specific risks, not stakeholder analysis.
whyNot.1: The project management team structure shows the project's roles and how they relate; it does not analyse who is impacted or influential.
whyNot.2: The issue management approach describes how issues are captured and changes to baselines are controlled.

B.q:
Which two statements about communication in PRINCE2 7 are correct?
1. The communication management approach is part of the PID.
2. Communication is a one-way flow from the project board to stakeholders.
3. Pockets of resistance show where communication should be focused.
4. The communication management approach is set out by the business layer in the mandate.
B.why: The approach is part of the PID (1), and resistance indicates where communication should be focused (3) (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: PRINCE2 calls for a controlled, bidirectional flow that includes feedback.
whyNot.2: Both are false: communication is two-way, and the approach is created in initiating a project, not in the mandate.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the approach is agreed in initiation as one of the management approaches in the PID.

B.q: Under which heading of the communication management approach should 'a video meeting platform for the hybrid team' be recorded?
B.why: Communications platforms and tools for analytics or automation go under supporting tools and techniques (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Resources covers the people, time and money for communication activities; a platform is a tool.
whyNot.1: Stakeholder analysis identifies who is impacted and who can influence the project.
whyNot.2: The schedule sets the purpose, frequency, channel and messages for each stakeholder group, not the software used.

B.q: A respected branch manager keeps objecting to a project's plans in meetings. What does PRINCE2 suggest the project manager does?
options: Focus communication on him to understand why he resists
Leave him off the distribution list to protect morale
Ask the executive to drop him from the stakeholder list
Log his objections as a risk and carry on as planned
B.why: Pockets of resistance indicate where communication should be focused; the reasons for resistance should be found out, as they may be valid (manual 3.4).

whyNot.1: Excluding him removes the two-way flow and leaves his concerns unexplored.
whyNot.2: He can affect the project, so he remains a stakeholder whatever his view.
whyNot.3: Logging and carrying on does not find out why he resists, which is what PRINCE2 recommends.

C.q: In which process is the communication management approach first created, and where is it held?
options: Starting up a project; held in the project brief
Directing a project; held in the project mandate
Initiating a project; held in the PID
Managing a stage boundary; held in the end stage report
C.why: It is created in initiating a project, in 'agree the management approaches', and forms part of the PID.

whyNot.0: Starting up a project produces the project brief; the management approaches are agreed in initiation.
whyNot.1: The mandate comes from the business layer before the project starts; it does not hold the management approaches.
whyNot.3: The approach is reviewed at stage boundaries, but it is created in initiation and held in the PID.

C.q: A project's highlight reports are sent to the board every fortnight. Where is this reporting frequency defined?
C.why: In 'report highlights', the project manager produces highlight reports at the frequency set in the communication management approach (manual 16.4.8).

whyNot.0: The stage plan sets out the stage's products, activities and timings, not the reporting frequency.
whyNot.2: The issue management approach covers issues and change control, not routine reporting frequency.
whyNot.3: The project management team structure sets out the project's roles and how they relate, not how often highlight reports are sent.

C.q: At the end of stage 2, the project manager learns that a regulator has become interested in the project. What should happen to the communication management approach, and when?
options: Leave it until closure, when stakeholders are notified
Replace it with an exception plan raised in controlling a stage
Pass it to the business layer to reissue with the mandate
Review and update it in managing a stage boundary
C.why: Management approaches, including the communication management approach, are reviewed and adapted at stage boundaries as stakeholders and relationships change.

whyNot.0: Waiting until closure leaves a new stakeholder unplanned for during the remaining stages.
whyNot.1: Exception plans respond to forecast tolerance breaches and are prepared in managing a stage boundary, not controlling a stage.
whyNot.2: The mandate is the business layer's trigger for the project; it is not where the approach is updated.

reteach.title: Planning a wedding's communications
reteach.question: How do you make sure 120 guests turn up at the right place, on the right day, without confusion?

blocks.body: First, work out who needs to know and who could cause trouble (stakeholder analysis). Then plan what each group hears, how and when: save-the-date, invitation, reminder (schedule). Choose a wedding website and RSVP form (tools). Ask your sister to spend an evening a week chasing replies (resources). When Uncle Ray grumbles about the venue, call him and find out why.

head: Wedding
Heading
rows: Guest list and who might object

blocks.text: The wedding website is a tool, not a resource. Resources are the people, time and money spent on communicating.

explain.body: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, across the project ecosystem. It is part of the PID.

test.q: Which best describes what the communication management approach defines?
options: Means and frequency of communication and feedback
Procedures for capturing and assessing issues
Target state and the enabling transition activities
Quality methods and responsibilities for products
test.why: It defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem (manual 3.4).

whyNot.1: Capturing and assessing issues is covered by the issue management approach.
whyNot.2: Target state and transition belong to the change management approach.
whyNot.3: Quality methods and responsibilities belong to the quality management approach.

explain.body: This heading identifies and analyses those impacted by the project's outcome or by the delivery process, and those who can influence its success or failure.

test.q: Which heading records who is affected by the project and who can influence its success?
test.why: Stakeholder analysis identifies who is impacted and who has influence (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Resources covers people, time and money for communications.
whyNot.1: The schedule sets purpose, frequency, channel and message for each group.
whyNot.3: Supporting tools covers platforms and analytics or automation tools.

explain.body: Pockets of resistance are a useful indicator of where communication should be focused. Find out why people resist; they may have a valid reason.

test.q: What do pockets of resistance to the project indicate?
options: Stakeholders to remove from the analysis
A forecast breach of stage tolerance
A need for premature project closure
test.why: PRINCE2 treats resistance as an indicator of where to focus communication (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Resistant stakeholders still affect the project and stay in the analysis.
whyNot.2: A forecast tolerance breach is a progress matter shown by figures, not by resistance.
whyNot.3: Premature closure is a board decision when the project is no longer justified.

explain.body: The approach is created in initiation, used during each stage (for example to set highlight report frequency), adapted at stage boundaries and reviewed at closure to decide who needs to be told.

test.q: When should the communication management approach be reviewed and, if needed, adapted?
options: When the project mandate is issued
At stage boundaries and at closure
test.why: The approach is adapted at stage boundaries and reviewed at closure for who to notify.

whyNot.0: Checkpoint reports are team manager progress reports on work packages.
whyNot.1: An off-specification is an issue handled under the issues practice.
whyNot.2: The mandate is issued before the approach exists; it is created in initiation.
